# Schemas: editors from annotations

Mods `schema_base` (the model), `schema_tools` (the Data Editor window and the command palette); read by the
validator and the item and character editors.

RPG Maker's plugins describe their parameters in comments (`@param`, `@type`) and its editor builds forms
from them. Here the same idea is data: a mod ships `schemas/<mod>.json` that describes its scenario
actions, its DSL commands and the fields of entity kinds. Those can be its own kinds or anyone else's. The
tools merge every mod's schema and build forms, pickers and checks from it.

## A schema file

```jsonc
{
  "Actions": [{
    "Id": "stat.add", "Name": "stats/schema/stat_add", "Category": "stats",
    "Params": [
      { "Key": "stat", "Type": "ref", "Kind": "stat", "Required": true, "Name": "stats/schema/field/stat" },
      { "Key": "value", "Type": "formula" },
      { "Key": "who", "Type": "who" }
    ]
  }],
  "Commands": [{
    "Id": "check", "Arrow": "checks/schema/arrow_success",
    "Positional": [{ "Key": "stat", "Type": "ref", "Kind": "stat", "Required": true }, { "Key": "dc", "Type": "int", "Required": true }],
    "Params": [{ "Key": "else", "Type": "label" }, { "Key": "dice", "Type": "text" }]
  }],
  "Kinds": [{
    // Adds fields to someone else's kind: every item now has an equip type and traits in the editors
    "Kind": "item",
    "Fields": [
      { "Key": "Equip", "Type": "text" },
      { "Key": "Traits", "Type": "list", "Of": [{ "Key": "Stat", "Type": "ref", "Kind": "stat" }, { "Key": "Add", "Type": "number" }] }
    ]
  }]
}
```

Field types: `text`, `locale`, `int`, `number`, `bool`, `choice` (`Options`), `ref` / `ref_list` (`Kind`),
`who`, `picture` (`Group`), `formula`, `condition`, `scene`, `flag`, `label`, `list` (`Of`), `map`, `pick` (`Kind` + `From`), `stages`, `json`. Unknown types fall back to text. `pick` gathers a field's values across entities (for example accepted equipment types) rather than naming an entity. `stages` edits quest step numbers and localized texts. `choice` accepts a named option or a zero-based numeric option index; serialized numeric enums need not become strings.
`Name` and `Description` are locale keys of your own mod.

Schemas merge in mod load order. An action or command is replaced whole. A kind is merged field by field,
so two mods can each add their own fields to `item`.

Each engine mod describes its own actions next to its code: `dialog_base` its commands (`text`, `select`,
`option` with `if`, `when`, …), `items_base` `item.add`, `trading` `trade.open`, `rpg` `rpg.teleport` and its battles integration `rpg.battle`, `quests_base` the `quest.*` actions, and so on.

## What you get from it

- **Data Editor** window (tool `schema_data_editor`): the described kinds on the left, the entities of a mod
  in the middle, and a form of every mod's fields on the right. Pickers list real entities (stats, classes,
  items, scenes). Texts are entered in every language of the mod. Save writes JSON, and the running game
  sees the change at once.
- **Command palette** (tool `schema_palette`): find any action or command, fill in its form, see the
  finished line and its check, and insert it into the open scenario. The text stays the source.
- **Item and character editors** show other mods' fields of their kind in a "Fields of other mods"
  section. Install `equipment` and the item editor gains Equip and Traits.
- **Validator**: unknown and missing parameters, bad numbers and choices, references to entities that do
  not exist, unparsable conditions in `option … if=` and `when`. The resource atlas sees the references too.

## Foreign entries, field patches and renaming

The Data Editor can include entries of the chosen mod's dependencies. Editing one writes `patches/<kind>/<chosen_mod>.json` containing only changed fields; **Reset to inherited** removes the local patch, and the per-field reset removes that override. Unknown fields are preserved.

**Rename…** previews changed references within the chosen mod and separately lists references from other mods. Confirming writes the local transaction only; other mods are not rewritten. **Undo rename** restores the prior files. Items and Characters editors use the same service. This is entity renaming, not a promise that RPG map/placement identifiers and save data are migrated.

## Your own mechanic

Write the C# action or the entity kind as usual, then add `schemas/<your_mod>.json` and its locale keys.
No editor code is needed: the Data Editor, the palette and the validator pick it up on the next start.

# Mod Settings

Mods can expose user-configurable settings that appear in the in-game settings menu under a dedicated "Mod Settings" tab. The UI shows a vertical list of mods (only those that have settings) on the left; clicking a mod name displays its settings controls on the right.

## Architecture

The system mirrors the save system (`IModSaveable`) using a similar dispatch pattern:

```
Mod assembly loaded
  → ModSettingsRegistry.RegisterAssembly(assembly, modId)
    → Finds IModSettings implementation via reflection
    → Stores (modId, instance) pair

Boot time:
  → ModSettingsRegistry.LoadAll()
    → For each registered mod: load user://mod_settings/{modId}.json
    → Call mod.ReadValues(blob)

Settings menu opened:
  → ModSettingsRegistry.GetModsWithSettings()
    → Returns sorted list of mod IDs (only mods with IModSettings)
  → BuildModList() — creates buttons in left panel
  → On click: BuildModSettingsPanel(modId)
    → mod.GetDefinitions() → list of ModSettingDefinition
    → Creates UI controls (CheckButton, SpinBox, OptionButton, etc.)
    → mod.WriteValues(blob) → populates controls with current values

Setting changed:
  → Read all control values into DataBlob
  → ModSettingsRegistry.SaveModSettings(modId, blob)
  → ModSettingsRegistry.ApplyValues(modId, blob)
    → mod.ReadValues(blob) — immediate apply

Reset:
  → ModSettingsRegistry.DeleteModSettings(modId)
  → Rebuild panel with DefaultValues from definitions
```

## Core concepts

### IModSettings interface

Mods implement one class implementing `IModSettings`. It is auto-discovered when the mod assembly loads.

```csharp
public interface IModSettings
{
    IReadOnlyList<ModSettingDefinition> GetDefinitions();
    void WriteValues(DataBlob blob);
    void ReadValues(DataBlob blob);
}
```

- **GetDefinitions()** — Declares which settings the mod has. Called every time the settings panel opens.
- **WriteValues(blob)** — The mod writes its current values into the blob. Called to populate UI controls and to persist.
- **ReadValues(blob)** — The mod reads values from the blob and applies them. Called on boot (from persisted data) and on every UI change.

### ModSettingDefinition

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Key` | `string` | Unique key within this mod (e.g. `"atb_speed"`) |
| `Name` | `string` | Localisation key shown as label (e.g. `"mod_ffbattle/atb_speed"`) |
| `Type` | `SettingType` | Widget type: `Bool`, `Integer`, `Float`, `String`, `Enum`, `Slider` |
| `DefaultValue` | `string` | String representation of the default. Used when no persisted value exists and on Reset |
| `Options` | `Dict<string,string>` | For `Enum` only: maps internal values to localisation keys |
| `Min` / `Max` / `Step`| `float` | For `Slider` only |

### Setting types and UI controls

| Type | Godot control | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Bool` | `CheckButton` | On/off toggle |
| `Integer` | `SpinBox` (step=1) | Whole-number input |
| `Float` | `SpinBox` (step=0.1) | Decimal input |
| `String` | `LineEdit` | Free-form text input |
| `Enum` | `OptionButton` | Dropdown, populated from `Options` dictionary |
| `Slider` | `HSlider` + value label | Range slider with configurable min/max/step |

### Persistence

Each mod's settings are stored as a JSON-serialised `DataBlob` at `user://mod_settings/{modId}.json`. The file contains key-value pairs matching the mod's definitions.

The core handles all file I/O; the mod never touches the filesystem.

### Lifecycle

```
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Boot                                                         │
│   ModRegistry.Initialize()                                   │
│     → ModAssemblyLoader.RegisterAssembly()                   │
│       → ModSettingsRegistry.RegisterAssembly(asm, modId)     │
│         → Finds IModSettings, instantiates, stores           │
│   SceneManager.Initialize()                                  │
│     → ModInitializerRegistry.NotifyResourcesReady()          │
│     → ModSettingsRegistry.LoadAll()                          │
│       → For each mod: loads JSON, calls ReadValues()         │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                              │
┌─────────────────────────────▼────────────────────────────────┐
│ Settings menu opened                                         │
│   BuildModList()                                             │
│     → GetModsWithSettings() → buttons in list                │
│   Select first mod                                           │
│   BuildModSettingsPanel(modId)                               │
│     → GetDefinitions() → controls in right panel             │
│     → WriteValues(blob) → populate controls                  │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                              │
┌─────────────────────────────▼────────────────────────────────┐
│ User changes a setting                                       │
│   OnModSettingChanged()                                      │
│     → Read all controls → DataBlob                           │
│     → SaveModSettings(modId, blob) → disk                    │
│     → ApplyValues(modId, blob) → mod.ReadValues()            │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## Implementing IModSettings in a mod

### Minimal example — simple toggles and sliders

```csharp
using System.Collections.Generic;
using Cthangover.Core.Mods;
using Cthangover.Core.Settings;

public class MyModSettings : IModSettings
{
    private float _explosionRadius = 1.5f;
    private bool _debugMode;

    public IReadOnlyList<ModSettingDefinition> GetDefinitions()
    {
        return new List<ModSettingDefinition>
        {
            new()
            {
                Key = "explosion_radius",
                Name = "mymod/explosion_radius",
                Type = SettingType.Slider,
                DefaultValue = "1.5",
                Min = 0.5f,
                Max = 10f,
                Step = 0.5f
            },
            new()
            {
                Key = "debug_mode",
                Name = "mymod/debug_mode",
                Type = SettingType.Bool,
                DefaultValue = "false"
            }
        };
    }

    public void WriteValues(DataBlob blob)
    {
        blob.SetFloat("explosion_radius", _explosionRadius);
        blob.SetBool("debug_mode", _debugMode);
    }

    public void ReadValues(DataBlob blob)
    {
        _explosionRadius = blob.GetFloat("explosion_radius", 1.5f);
        _debugMode = blob.GetBool("debug_mode", false);
    }
}
```

![Mod Settings example view](mod_example.png)

### Example with enum

```csharp
new ModSettingDefinition
{
    Key = "difficulty",
    Name = "mymod/difficulty",
    Type = SettingType.Enum,
    DefaultValue = "normal",
    Options = new Dictionary<string, string>
    {
        { "easy",   "mymod/diff_easy" },
        { "normal", "mymod/diff_normal" },
        { "hard",   "mymod/diff_hard" }
    }
}
```

![Mod Settings example view](mod_example_enum.png)

The `Options` dictionary maps internal values (stored in the blob) to localisation keys (shown in the dropdown). The mod provides translations in its `locale/` files.

### Localisation

Every `Name` field and every value in `Options` is a localisation key resolved via `TranslationServer.Translate()`. Add entries to your mod's `locale/` files:

```
# locale/en.properties
mymod/explosion_radius = Explosion Radius
mymod/debug_mode = Debug Mode
mymod/difficulty = Difficulty
mymod/diff_easy = Easy
mymod/diff_normal = Normal
mymod/diff_hard = Hard
```

### Schema changes

**`DataBlob.Version` is NOT persisted for mod settings.** `ModSettingsRegistry.SaveModSettings` writes only the key-value payload (`blob.GetBytes()`), and on load the registry constructs a fresh `DataBlob(payload)`, which resets `Version` to its default of 1. (`Version` *is* persisted through the main save system's `SavePackage` — just not here.)

Detect schema changes by reading keys with defaults instead — missing keys resolve to your fallback values, so added fields need no migration logic:

```csharp
public void WriteValues(DataBlob blob)
{
    blob.SetFloat("explosion_radius", _explosionRadius);
    blob.SetFloat("knockback_force", _knockbackForce); // added later
}

public void ReadValues(DataBlob blob)
{
    _explosionRadius = blob.GetFloat("explosion_radius", 1.5f);
    _knockbackForce = blob.GetFloat("knockback_force", 3.0f); // default for old saves
}
```

## Important rules

- **One `IModSettings` per mod** — create a single implementation in your assembly.
- **Always provide `DefaultValue`** — used when no persisted value exists and on Reset.
- **Use `DataBlob` key-value API** — `GetInt/SetInt`, `GetFloat/SetFloat`, `GetString/SetString`, `GetBool/SetBool`.
- **Always call with defaults** — `blob.GetInt("key", defaultVal)` so missing keys don't break.
- **Key names are persistent** — changing a `Key` creates a new setting; the old value is lost.
- **Provide localisation** — add translations for all `Name` and `Options` values in `locale/`.
- **The `version` field in `manifest.json`** is used by the save system for validation; mod settings have no persisted schema version (`DataBlob.Version` is reset to 1 on load) — handle schema changes via read-with-defaults.
- **Declare `"sources"` in manifest.json** — your `.cs` files must be listed in the `sources` field of `manifest.json` for the compiler to pick them up. See [Manifest — sources](../configs/index.md#manifestjson) for details.

# Skills

Skills are card-based abilities that characters can acquire, equip, and use in battle. Defined as JSON data and rendered as skill cards in the UI.

## JSON structure

```jsonc
{
  // Unique skill ID — used for lookups and save data
  "Id": "slave_master",
  // Locale key for the skill's display name on the card
  "Name": "skills/slave_master/name",
  // Locale key for the skill's tooltip/description text
  "Description": "skills/slave_master/desc",
  // Path to card artwork sprite, resolved from the characters/skills mod group
  "Image": "slave_master",
  // Skill activation type: "Active", "Passive", or "ForCharacter"
  "Type": "Passive",
  // Rarity tier: "Common", "Uncommon", "Rare", "Epic", or "Legendary"
  "Rare": "Legendary",
  // Optional: action card granted to the player when the skill is acquired
  // (active skills hand over a card this way)
  "GrantsAction": "physics/attack",
  // Optional: numeric stat bonuses while the skill is owned
  "Effects": [
    { "Key": "characters/skills/effects/recruit", "Value": 10, "Percent": true }
  ]
}
```

## Field reference

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Id` | string | Unique skill ID used for lookups and save data |
| `Name` | string | Locale key for display name |
| `Description` | string | Locale key for tooltip/description text |
| `Image` | string | Path to skill card artwork, resolved from mod group `characters/skills` |
| `Type` | string | `"Active"`, `"Passive"`, or `"ForCharacter"` |
| `Rare` | string | `"Common"`, `"Uncommon"`, `"Rare"`, `"Epic"`, or `"Legendary"` |
| `GrantsAction` | string | Optional action card ID pushed into the action pool when the skill is granted |
| `Effects` | array of objects | Optional numeric bonuses granted while the skill is owned — see below |

## Skill types

### `Active`
Must be intentionally triggered during the player's turn, consuming an action resource and targeting a specific ally or enemy. Active skills appear as cards in the player's hand.

### `Passive`
Remains in effect continuously once acquired. Provides a persistent buff or aura without requiring player input. Passive skills do not appear in the hand — they are always active.

### `ForCharacter`
Applies directly to the owning character as a stat modifier or intrinsic trait. These are character-specific upgrades that modify base stats.

### `Effects` — collection bonuses

Each effect is one numeric bonus: `Key` is the locale key naming the affected
stat (e.g. `characters/skills/effects/recruit`), `Value` is the magnitude
(negative values are penalties), and `Percent` selects the display unit
(`+10%` vs `+10`). Effects sharing a `Key` are summed across every owned
skill by `SkillEffectAggregator` into the skills panel's global "collection
effect" plate — so one key must keep the same unit across all skills. The
reference definition `cthangover_game/characters/skills/slave_master.json`
ships one effect: `+10%` recruitment (`"Value": 10, "Percent": true`).

## Granting action cards

An active skill hands the player an action card instead of acting by itself: set `GrantsAction` to the action's `Id`. When the skill is granted, `SkillService` adds the skill to the owned set and appends the card to the action pool, where it can be assigned to a character in the character panel. The skills panel shows the pairing — opening the skill displays "grants an action card" with the card's icon and name.

Granting is idempotent: an already owned skill is ignored, so replaying a scenario event cannot duplicate the card. Action cards awarded this way are not destroyed by the character panel's reset button — reset restores template assignments and returns awarded cards to the pool.

## Rarity tiers

| Tier | Description |
|---|---|
| `Common` | Standard skill — highest drop rate, baseline power |
| `Uncommon` | Slightly improved stats, lower drop rate |
| `Rare` | Notably stronger, appears infrequently |
| `Epic` | Powerful skill with significant gameplay impact, very low drop chance |
| `Legendary` | Game-changing abilities, extremely rare acquisition |

The rarity tier drives the visual frame colour on the skill card via `SkillCardFrameBehaviour`.

## Skill data at runtime

Skill ownership is tracked in `SkillData`:

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `HasSkill(id)` | Check if the player owns a skill |
| `AddSkill(id)` | Add a skill to the player's collection (no card grants — prefer `SkillService`) |

Acquisitions go through `SkillService.GrantSkill(id)`, which pairs the skill with its `GrantsAction` card. From a scenario:

```scenario
action character.add_skill skill_id=slave_master
```

The scenario action rejects unknown skill IDs with a log warning and does nothing when the skill is already owned.

## Skill file format

Skill files are self-describing envelopes routed by `Kind`, with no index file:

```jsonc
{
  // Skills are a separate entity kind, not part of characters
  "Kind": "skill",
  "Items": [
    {
      "Id": "slave_master",
      "Name": "characters/skills/slave_master_name",
      "Description": "characters/skills/slave_master",
      "Image": "characters/skills/slave_master",
      "Type": 1,
      "Rare": 3
    }
  ]
}
```

A mod may place this file anywhere; the entity resolver finds it by kind.

## Locale keys

```properties
skills/slave_master/name = Slave Master
skills/slave_master/desc = Increases recruitment chance against defeated enemies by 25%
```

## UI components

| Class | Description |
|---|---|
| `SkillCardBehaviour` | Individual skill card rendering |
| `SkillCardFrameBehaviour` | Card frame with rarity-based colouring |
| `SkillWidget` | Compact skill display widget |
| `SkillsPanelBehaviour` | Skills management panel in game UI |

# Sounds — Sound Effects

One-shot sound effect files (`.ogg` / `.wav`) organized by category, referenced from scenarios via the `sound` command.

## Directory structure

```filestree
sounds/
├── battle/           # combat sounds
│   ├── hit.ogg
│   ├── damage.ogg
│   └── stun.ogg
├── locations/        # ambient location sounds
│   ├── door_open.ogg
│   └── fire_crackle.ogg
├── ui/               # interface feedback
│   ├── click.ogg
│   ├── hover.ogg
│   └── notification.ogg
└── record_scratch.ogg
```

## File format

- `.ogg` (Vorbis) and `.wav` are accepted. Although `audio_extensions` exists in the config DTO, the current runtime loader retains this default list; changing that JSON field alone does not enable another format.
- Short duration (0.1–5 seconds) recommended for one-shot effects
- The sound id is the path relative to the mod's `sounds/` folder, minus extension: `sounds/ui/click.ogg` → `ui/click`, `battle/hit`

## Real example — `cthangover_game/sounds/`

From `mods/cthangover_game/sounds/`:

```filestree
sounds/
├── record_scratch.ogg         # comedic timing effect
├── battle/
│   ├── physics_damage.ogg
│   ├── physics_defence.ogg
│   ├── death.ogg
│   └── stun_apply.ogg
├── locations/
│   ├── door_creak.ogg
│   └── wind_ambient.ogg
└── ui/
    ├── button_click.ogg
    ├── notification_chime.ogg
    └── quest_update.ogg
```

## Real example — `card_battle/sounds/`

From `mods/card_battle/sounds/`:

```filestree
sounds/
├── card_pick.ogg              # picking up a card
├── card_drop.ogg              # placing a card on target
├── card_damage.ogg            # damage number appears
├── card_stun.ogg              # stun effect applied
├── card_death.ogg             # card death dissolve
├── turn_start.ogg             # new turn
└── turn_end.ogg               # end turn button
```

## Usage in scenarios

```scenario
sound ui/click
text "- ..." key=dialogue_line
sound battle/hit
delay 0.5
sound ui/notification_chime
```

- `sound` plays immediately and does not block script execution
- Multiple sounds can play simultaneously
- The engine manages audio channels and prevents clipping

## Usage from C#

Sounds are played through `Cthangover.Core.Audio.IAudioService` (implemented by `AudioService`):

```csharp
var audio = GetNodeOrNull<AudioService>("/root/AudioService");

// Exact id
audio.PlaySound("ui/click", SoundType.UI);

// With random variations: picks "battle/hit_1" .. "battle/hit_3"
audio.PlaySound("battle/hit", 3, SoundType.Timed);
```

`SoundType` selects the playback pool — each type gets its own player, so a new
`CardEffect` sound cuts the previous one while a `UI` sound plays independently:
`Timed`, `Background`, `Foreground`, `UI`, `Notification`, `CardEffect`, `CardAction`.

### Engine internals

A few extra members on `AudioService` are useful for mod code:

- `IsMusicPlaying()` — returns `true` when the dedicated Music player is
  currently producing audio; lets UI display playback state without touching
  the player node directly
- `static LinearToDb(float linear)` — public helper converting a linear
  amplitude (0–1) to decibels via `20 * log10(linear)`, clamped to −80 dB at
  the bottom so zero never becomes `-infinity`
- `MixerType` enum (`Sounds`, `Musics`, `Ambient`) — identifies the three audio
  buses (SFX / Music / Ambient) used by `SetVolume(MixerType, float)` and
  `SetEnabled(MixerType, bool)` for per-bus volume and mute control

## Adding a new sound

1. Place the `.ogg` or `.wav` file in `sounds/{category}/`
2. Reference in scenario: `sound category/filename` (no extension)
3. No config or registration needed — audio files are discovered at load time

## Sound categories

Categories are organizational, not enforced. Use whatever folder structure fits your mod:

| Category | Typical use |
|---|---|
| `battle/` | Combat sounds: hits, blocks, stuns, death |
| `locations/` | Environmental: doors, water, wind, fire |
| `ui/` | Interface feedback: clicks, hovers, notifications |
| `music/` | Note: music tracks go in `music/`, not `sounds/` |

For music / ambient tracks, use `music/` and the `music`/`music_play`/`music_pause` scenario commands instead. See `musics/` documentation.

# Scenario Actions

A GDScript that has both `get_name()` and `run(ctx)` is registered as a **scenario action**. The `ctx` parameter is a `GDActionContext` providing access to all game subsystems.

## Minimal action

`scripts/greet.gd`:
```gdscript
extends RefCounted

func get_name():
    return "my.hello"

func run(ctx):
    ctx.Log("EVENT", "Hello from GDScript!")
```

Usage in `.scenario`:
```scenario
action my.hello
```

## Action with parameters

```gdscript
extends RefCounted

func get_name():
    return "my.announce"

func run(ctx):
    var name = ctx.GetParam("name")
    var count = ctx.GetParam("count")
    if name == "":
        name = "Unknown"
    ctx.Log("EVENT", "Announcing: " + name + " x" + count)
```

```scenario
action my.announce name=Marao count=3
```

## Action context (GDActionContext) API

The `ctx` object provides these properties and methods:

| Member | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `GetParam(name)` | `string` | Read a parameter passed via `key=value` in the DSL |
| `Log(category, msg)` | `void` | Debug-level log |
| `LogWarning(category, msg)` | `void` | Warning-level log |
| `Quests` | `GDQuestService` | Full quest subsystem API |
| `Character` | `GDCharacterService` | Character party management |
| `Battle` | `GDBattleService` | Battle initiation |
| `Lighting` | `GDLightingService` | Lighting/depth map control |
| `Scene` | `GDSceneNodeService` | Scene node instantiation/removal |
| `Inventory` | `GDInventoryService` | Player inventory queries and mutations |
| `ModRegistry` | `GDModRegistryService` | Loaded mod introspection |
| `PublishEvent(key, data)` | `void` | Publish an event to the global event bus (see [Events](../../events/)) |

## Service API reference

### GDQuestService

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `Exists(id)` | Check if a quest is registered |
| `SetStatus(id, status)` | Set quest lifecycle state (e.g. `"Active"`, `"Completed"`) |
| `SetDataStatus(id, level)` | Set numeric progress counter |
| `AddTag(id, tag)` | Attach a tag for conditional logic |
| `RemoveTag(id, tag)` | Remove a tag |
| `SendNotification(id)` | Trigger "Quest Updated" UI popup |

```gdscript
func run(ctx):
    var qid = ctx.GetParam("quest_id")
    if ctx.Quests.Exists(qid):
        ctx.Quests.SetStatus(qid, "Active")
        ctx.Quests.AddTag(qid, "started_by_gd")
        ctx.Quests.SendNotification(qid)
```

### GDCharacterService

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `AddToParty(type)` | Add a character to the player's party |
| `SendNotification(type)` | Show "new party member" UI popup |

### GDBattleService

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `Init(sceneType, enemies, questId, newTag)` | Construct battle data and prepare encounter |

Pass empty strings `""` for `questId`/`newTag` to omit them.

### GDLightingService

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `ClearDepthMap()` | Reset lighting depth/albedo maps |
| `SetUseTime(useTime)` | Enable/disable time-of-day lighting |

### GDSceneNodeService

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `Instantiate(scenePath, nodeName)` | Load a PackedScene and add to scene tree |
| `Remove(nodeName)` | Remove and free a named node |

### GDInventoryService

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `HasItem(id)` | Check if item exists in inventory |
| `CheckCount(id)` | Get stack count of an item |
| `Add(id, count)` | Add items (default count=1) |
| `Remove(id, count)` | Remove items (returns `true` on success) |

### GDModRegistryService

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `IsLoaded(modId)` | Check if a mod is loaded |
| `GetOrderedModIds()` | Get ordered list of loaded mod IDs |

## Full action example

```gdscript
extends RefCounted

func get_name():
    return "my.quest_and_char"

func run(ctx):
    var quest = ctx.GetParam("quest_id")
    var hero = ctx.GetParam("hero")

    ctx.Quests.SetStatus(quest, "Active")
    ctx.Quests.AddTag(quest, "gds_managed")
    ctx.Quests.SendNotification(quest)

    ctx.Character.AddToParty(hero)
    ctx.Character.SendNotification(hero)

    if ctx.ModRegistry.IsLoaded("cthangover_game"):
        ctx.Log("EVENT", "Core is loaded, all good")
```

# Battle Action Executors

A GDScript that has both `get_action_id()` and `execute(action, user, target)` is registered as a **battle action executor**. The `action_id` must match an `ActionCharacter.ID` in the character's JSON data.

Recognition and registration happen in the turn-battle mod: `TurnBattleGDScriptHook` is installed into the core's `GDScriptHookRegistry`, which `ModGDScriptLoader` offers every compiled `.gd` file. A script that returns a dictionary from `execute` is wrapped in `GDBattleActionExecutor` and added to the global `ActionExecutorHub` pool.

## Executor contract

Arguments are plain Godot dictionaries — mod-authored C# classes get no Godot source generation, so custom RefCounted DTOs would be invisible to GDScript.

```gdscript
extends RefCounted

func get_action_id():
    return "my.custom_attack"

func execute(action, user, target):
    var damage = user["attack_value"] * 2 - target["defence_value"]
    if damage < 1:
        damage = 1

    return {
        "target_damage": damage,
        "target_defence": target["defence_value"],
        "result": true,
    }
```

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `action` | `Dictionary` | The ActionCharacter definition (`id`, `name`, `description`, `type`, `properties`) |
| `user` | `Dictionary` | The character performing the action |
| `target` | `Dictionary` | The character receiving the action |

## `action` fields

| Field | Type |
|---|---|
| `id` | `String` |
| `name` | `String` |
| `description` | `String` |
| `type` | `int` |
| `properties` | `Dictionary` (string → string, the raw `PropertyData` bag) |

## Character fields

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `String` | Character identifier |
| `name` | `String` | Display name |
| `level` | `int` | Current level |
| `exp` | `int` | Experience points |
| `recruitment_chance` | `int` | Recruitment chance (0-100) |
| `health_value` / `health_max` | `int` | Current / max health |
| `defence_value` / `defence_max` | `int` | Current / max defence |
| `attack_value` / `attack_max` | `int` | Current / max attack |
| `point_value` / `point_max` | `int` | Current / max action points |
| `properties` | `Dictionary` | Raw string properties (`Speed`, `StunImmune`, …) |

## Return value

`execute` must return a `Dictionary`. Missing keys default to zero; `result` defaults to `true`, so a script that only reports deltas counts as a successful action.

| Key | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `source_damage` | `int` | Damage dealt by the source |
| `source_defence` | `int` | Source defence delta |
| `target_damage` | `int` | Damage dealt to the target |
| `target_defence` | `int` | Target defence delta |
| `result` | `bool` | Whether the action succeeded (default `true`) |

A script that returns a non-dictionary value yields a failed result (`Result = false`), so one broken mod cannot abort the action pipeline.
mods/src/gdscript/conditions:
# Custom Conditions

A GDScript that has both `get_condition_name()` and `evaluate(flags, args)` is registered as a **custom condition leaf parser**. Conditions can be used in the `condition:` metadata field of `.scenario` files.

## Minimal condition

`scripts/weather_check.gd`:
```gdscript
extends RefCounted

func get_condition_name():
    return "gds.is_rain"

func evaluate(flags, args):
    return flags.get("weather", "") == "rain"
```

Usage:
```scenario
scene: town_entry
priority: 5
condition: gds.is_rain
---
text "It's pouring outside."
end
```

## Condition with arguments

Arguments passed in parentheses become integer-keyed entries in the `args` dictionary:

```gdscript
extends RefCounted

func get_condition_name():
    return "gds.flag_equals"

func evaluate(flags, args):
    var expected = args.get("0", "")
    if expected == "":
        return false
    return flags.get("custom_flag", "") == expected
```

```scenario
condition: gds.flag_equals("victory")
```

## Condition parameters

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `flags` | `Dictionary` | Scene flag dictionary (string → string). Populated by `set` DSL commands and action code. |
| `args` | `Dictionary` | Positional arguments from condition call (string index → string value). Empty if no parentheses. |
mods/src/gdscript/index:
# GDScript in Mods

Mods can include `.gd` (GDScript) files alongside or instead of C# source code. GDScript files are compiled by Godot's built-in GDScript engine and can implement scenario actions, custom conditions, battle action executors, item actions, mod initializers, and winground listeners — all without Roslyn or a C# toolchain.

## How it works

1. Mod manifest declares `"gd_sources": ["scripts/*.gd"]`
2. On mod load, the kernel finds `.gd` files, compiles them via `GDScript.Reload()`, instantiates, and inspects methods
3. If the GDScript has known method patterns, it is auto-registered into the corresponding subsystem
4. No manual registration code needed — the kernel does it automatically

## manifest.json — gd_sources field

```jsonc
{
  "id": "my_mod",                                          // Canonical mod identifier
  "name": "My GDScript Mod",                               // Human-readable mod name
  "version": "0.1.0",                                      // Semver version
  "gd_sources": ["scripts/*.gd"],                          // Glob patterns for .gd files
  "depends": ["cthangover_game>=0.1.0"]                                      // Versioned dependency strings
}
```

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| `gd_sources` | Glob patterns for `.gd` files |

> **Note on pattern matching:** despite the glob-like syntax, the directory walk is **always recursive**. A pattern like `scripts/*.gd` is split at the last `/`: the part before it (`scripts`) selects the root directory, and the suffix after it (`*.gd`) only acts as a **file name filter**. As a result, `scripts/*.gd` also picks up files such as `scripts/any/deep/foo.gd`. There is no way to limit matching to a single directory level; use distinct top-level folders if you need separation.

A single `.gd` file can implement multiple interfaces simultaneously — the kernel checks all known patterns on each script.

## Pages

- [Scenario Actions](actions.md) — actions + GDActionContext + service APIs
- [Custom Conditions](conditions.md) — condition leaf parsers
- [Battle Action Executors](battle.md) — custom battle logic
- [Item Actions](items.md) — item usage handlers
- [Mod Lifecycle](lifecycle.md) — initializers, event bus, publishing events

## Auto-detection summary

| GDScript methods | Registered as | Subsystem |
|---|---|---|
| `get_name()` + `run(ctx)` | `IScenarioAction` | Scenario action factory (`run` receives a GDScript action context) |
| `get_condition_name()` + `evaluate(flags, args)` | `ILeafParser` | Condition parser registry (priority over QuestParser) |
| `get_action_id()` + `execute(action, user, target)` | `IActionExecutor` | Battle action executor hub (global); returns a result object converted to attribute changes |
| `get_item_action_id()` + `use(item)` | `IItemAction` | Item action factory; `item` is a GDScript item wrapper, return `bool` |
| `on_mod_loaded(mod_id)` / `on_mod_resources_ready()` | `IModInitializer` | Mod initializer registry; `on_mod_loaded` receives the mod ID string |
| `get_winground_listener_id()` + optional `on_winground_before_exp(ctx)` / `on_winground_after_loot(ctx)` / `on_winground_before_show(ctx)` | `IWingroundListener` | Winground listener registry; all three hooks are optional and receive a context object synced back after the call |
| `on_mod_event_*` | String event subscriber | Global event bus |

Detection details:

- Scenario actions are detected by the presence of **`get_name()`** together with `run()` — there is no separate `get_action_name()` convention.
- Initializers register when *either* callback is present; each missing one is simply not invoked.
- Winground listeners register only if `get_winground_listener_id()` returns a non-empty ID in addition to at least one hook method.

A single `.gd` file can implement multiple patterns simultaneously.

## Order among C# and GDScript

1. C# assemblies are compiled and loaded first (via Roslyn or precompiled DLLs)
2. GDScript files are loaded second
3. All registrations happen during the same load phase

GDScript **conditions** use `RegisterFirst` — they are inserted at the front of the leaf parser list, taking priority over the built-in `QuestParser`. This means `gds.is_rain` resolves before the parser tries to interpret `gds` as a quest ID.

# Item Actions

A GDScript that has both `get_item_action_id()` and `use(item)` is registered as an **item action**. The ID must match an `ItemAction` field in the item's JSON definition.

```gdscript
extends RefCounted

func get_item_action_id():
    return "my.heal_potion"

func use(item):
    print("[ITEM] Using: " + item.Name + " (id=" + item.Id + ")")
    # Perform healing logic here
    return true
```

## GDItem fields

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Id` | `string` | Item identifier |
| `Name` | `string` | Display name |
| `Description` | `string` | Tooltip text |
| `Cost` | `int` | Purchase price |
| `ItemType` | `int` | Item category flags |
mods/src/gdscript/lifecycle:
# Mod Lifecycle

A GDScript with `on_mod_loaded(modId)` or `on_mod_resources_ready()` is registered as a **mod initializer**. The kernel calls these lifecycle hooks:

```gdscript
extends RefCounted

func on_mod_loaded(mod_id):
    print("[MY_MOD] on_mod_loaded: " + mod_id)

func on_mod_resources_ready():
    print("[MY_MOD] All mod resources are ready")
```

| Hook | Called when |
|---|---|
| `on_mod_loaded(modId)` | Another mod finishes loading. Called for every mod (including itself). |
| `on_mod_resources_ready()` | All mods and their JSON resources are fully loaded. Called once. |

## Event bus auto-registration (`on_mod_event_*`)

GDScript objects are automatically scanned for methods starting with `on_mod_event_`.
Each method is subscribed to the string event bus under the key after the prefix:

```gdscript
# scripts/quest_watcher.gd
func on_mod_event_quest_status_changed(data: Dictionary) -> void:
    if data.quest_id == "main_quest" and data.new_status == "completed":
        print("Quest completed!")

func on_mod_event_battle_ended(data: Dictionary) -> void:
    if data.result == "victory":
        heal_party()
```

The method receives a `Dictionary` with `snake_case` keys matching the event's
typed C# properties. See [Events](../../events/) for the full list of built-in events
and their payloads.

## Publishing events from scenario actions

Scenario action scripts can publish events via `ctx.PublishEvent()`:

```gdscript
func get_name() -> String:
    return "cooking.meal_cooked"

func run(ctx) -> void:
    ctx.PublishEvent("cooking_meal_ready", {
        "dish": ctx.GetParam("dish"),
        "quality": ctx.GetParam("quality")
    })
```

Other mods (C# or GDScript) can subscribe to this event by its string key.
See [Events](../../events/) for the full event bus API.

# Integrations, assembly consumers and reload

## Conditional integrations

An integration is glue that joins the loaded mod set only when its host and every named partner are present. It does not pull a partner into a game that did not select it. The host declares:

```json
{"integrations": [{"id": "battles", "with": ["turn_battle_base"]}]}
```

`integrations/battles/manifest.json` and its source/data files form the virtual mod `<host>__battles`. An optional `path` changes that folder. The virtual mod implicitly depends on its host and partners; its manifest can declare additional dependencies. It is not a separate player-toggleable mod card. Integrations are recomputed at boot and in-process game switches.

For example, `rpg__battles` connects the RPG world to turn-based battles and random encounters. `turn_battle_base__quests` applies battle results to quests. The `rpg` host can therefore be used without any battle engine, and the battle platform without quests. These are production integrations; `test_suites` are a separate opt-in test mechanism.

## Discovering extensions

`ModAssemblyLoader.RegisterAssembly(assembly, modId)` sends loaded assemblies through `AssemblyConsumerRegistry`. Kernel consumers cover actions, initializers, save/settings handlers, discovery, tools, scene events, TSCN building and asset resolvers. A subsystem owned by a mod can declare a public parameterless subclass of `ModTypeConsumer<T>` with a unique `Id`, `Add` and `Remove` methods.

The consumer receives implementations from already registered assemblies, including its own, and from later assemblies. Unloading calls `Remove` for exactly that assembly's contributions. Registries must release those instances and references; a static list retaining an unloaded implementation prevents collectible assemblies from being released. This mechanism is used by expression strategies, avatar renderer factories, atmosphere emitters and other mod-owned extension systems.

The namespace is `Cthangover.Core.Mods.Consumers`; source is `Core/Mods/Consumers/`. A new registry declares a consumer instead of inserting a subsystem-specific branch in the kernel's assembly loader. See [C# sources](index.md) for the other compilation contracts.

## Hot reload

When run from the Godot editor, file watching is enabled by default except for automated tests/atlas runs. Exported builds do not watch by default. `--hot-reload` opts in explicitly and `--no-hot-reload` wins over it. These are Godot user arguments after `--`.

The watcher considers source, manifests, data, scenes, locale and asset changes, while ignoring build folders, editor bookkeeping and temporary files. It prepares and compiles a candidate set before applying it. A rejected compile leaves the previous running version in place and reports the error. Applied changes go through normal unload and registration, and publish a mod-set reload event. Data changes invalidate the relevant resolvers.

Reloadable mods must unsubscribe events, free owned UI/native resources, release callbacks and discard old plugin instances on unload. Godot nodes, live avatar adapters and atmosphere emitters belong to their hosts; merely swapping an assembly does not transfer ownership. In-process game selection uses this same mod-set lifecycle, so test repeated game switches as well as initial boot.

Implementation: `Core/Mods/HotReload/`, `Core/Mods/Pipeline/ModSetReloader.cs`, `Core/Mods/ModIntegrations.cs`. The `hot_reload` and `resettables` suites exercise compile rejection and repeated switching.

# Stats, classes, checks and gear

Mods `stats_base`, `stat_checks`, `equipment`, `battle_formulas`; rules as data in `classic_rpg_pack`;
the sample game `rpg_plus`.

A stat is whatever your game counts: strength in an RPG, courage or trust in a visual novel. Nothing here
knows about tile maps, cards or novels, so the same character data works in a dialog, on a tile map and in
both battle cores. Everything below is JSON and scenario text; no C# is needed.

## Stats (`"Kind": "stat"`)

```jsonc
{
  "Kind": "stat",
  "Items": [
    // A base attribute: a number with a default and a lower bound
    { "Id": "str", "Name": "my/stat/str", "Short": "my/stat/str_short", "Group": "attributes", "Order": 1, "Default": 5, "Min": 1 },
    // A derived stat: a formula of other stats and the level, written into the battle's health
    { "Id": "hp", "Name": "my/stat/hp", "Group": "combat", "Order": 10, "Formula": "12 + vit * 3 + level * 2", "Min": 1, "Binds": "health" },
    // A pool: spent and refilled (mana). Battle actions pay with "Cost=mp:4"
    { "Id": "mp", "Name": "my/stat/mp", "Group": "combat", "Formula": "int * 2 + level * 2", "Pool": true }
  ]
}
```

`Binds` writes the stat into a battle attribute every core already reads: `health`, `attack`, `defence`,
`point`. `Group` and `Order` lay the stat out on the character sheet. `Hidden` keeps it off the sheet.

## Classes (`"Kind": "archetype"`)

An RPG class or a novel's temperament: stat values or formulas, traits, and actions learned on level-up.

```jsonc
{
  "Id": "classic/warrior",
  "Name": "classic/archetype/warrior",
  "Stats": { "str": "7 + level * 2", "vit": "6 + level * 2", "int": "2 + floor(level / 2)" },
  "Traits": [{ "Stat": "hp", "Percent": 10 }],
  "Learnings": [{ "Level": 1, "Action": "classic/power_strike" }, { "Level": 3, "Action": "classic/guard_break" }]
}
```

A character's own value wins over its class, the class over the stat's `Formula`, the formula over
`Default`. Then come permanent bonuses and traits: `(value + Add + Formula) × (1 + Percent / 100)`, clamped
to `Min`/`Max`.

## Traits on anything

Any entity can carry `"Traits"`: a character, an item, a class. The characters and items mods do not know
the key, so other mods' entities become stat-aware without changing their code. A patch gives stats to
someone else's character:

```jsonc
// patches/character.json of your mod: the wolf of another mod fights with a sheet
{ "Items": [{ "Id": "rpg_wolf", "Stats": { "str": 5, "vit": 5, "agi": 7 } }] }
```

## Formulas

`+ - * / % ^`, comparisons, `&& || !`, `cond ? a : b`, `min max floor ceil round abs sqrt clamp rand(lo, hi)
chance(p) if(c, a, b)`. Division by zero gives 0 and an unknown name reads 0, so a typo never crashes a
battle. The validator and the Data Editor window report it instead.

## Gear (`equipment`)

```jsonc
// Slots are data: what equip types a slot accepts
{ "Kind": "equip_slot", "Items": [{ "Id": "weapon", "Name": "classic/slot/weapon", "Accepts": ["sword", "staff", "dagger"] }] }

// An item becomes gear by its keys: "Equip" (its type), "Traits", "Archetypes" (who may wear it)
{ "Id": "classic/iron_sword", "Cost": 30, "ItemType": "TargetUsed", "ItemAction": "action/equip",
  "Equip": "sword", "Archetypes": ["classic/warrior", "classic/rogue"], "Traits": [{ "Stat": "atk", "Add": 5 }] }
```

`"ItemAction": "action/stat_up"` together with `"StatUp": { "str": 1 }` makes a tonic that adds permanent
bonuses.

## Skills with formulas (`battle_formulas`)

```jsonc
{ "Kind": "action", "Id": "classic/power_strike", "Type": "ToEnemy",
  "Values": ["RequiredPoint>=0.1.0", "Formula=a.atk * 1.5 + rand(0, a.str / 2)"] }
```

`a.*` is the one acting and `b.*` the target: their stats plus `hp`, `hp_max`, `attack`, `defence`, `point`.
Other values: `Effect=damage|heal`, `Cost=mp:4`, `Pierce>=0.1.0`, and `State=<status effect>` with
`StateTurns`/`StateChance`. Both battle cores run these skills.

## In scenarios

```text
action stat.add stat=cha value=1 who=player
action stat.archetype id=classic/rogue who=rpg_hero
action stat.exp value=20                       # the whole party by default
action equip.put item=classic/dagger who=rpg_hero give=1

check cha 10 who=rpg_hero else=snub -> :gift   # d20 + charisma against 10, shows the roll
when "level(rpg_hero) >= 3" -> :veteran else=rookie
select "What do you say?"
option "Bluff [Charisma]" "if=stat(rpg_hero, cha) >= 6" -> :bluff
option "Show the dagger" "if=equipped(rpg_hero, 'classic/dagger')" -> :threat
option "Leave" -> :leave
```

Conditions: `stat(who, stat) >= n`, `level(who) >= n`, `archetype(who, id)`, `equipped(who, item)`. They
work wherever conditions do: `when`, an `option`'s `if`, a scenario's `condition:`, map events. An option
whose condition is false is not offered. A choice with every option hidden is skipped.

`check` leaves `check_roll`, `check_total`, `check_dc`, `check_result` and more in the dialog variables for
your own lines. The dice default to the game setting `checks.dice`, else `d20`. `dice=none` makes a plain
threshold.

## Game settings (`collection.json` → `settings`)

| Setting | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `stats.player` | whose sheet `player` means |
| `stats.exp_curve` | exp needed for a level when the class has no `ExpCurve` |
| `stats.leveling` | `all` lets characters without a class level up too |
| `checks.dice` | default dice of `check` |

## The character sheet

The toolbar's book button shows the party, the class, the level and exp bar, the stats by group with the
part traits add, and blocks other mods add (the Equipment block with Take off). In C#, a mod adds a block by
implementing `ISheetSection`.

## See it working

`--game=rpg_plus --new`: a novel prologue picks the class and makes a charisma check, then the tile world
uses the same stats in gear, battles and the sheet. The content is in `mods/rpg_plus_game`, the rules in
`mods/classic_rpg_pack`.

# Status Effects

Status effects are temporary buffs, debuffs, or crowd-control effects applied to characters during battle. Defined as JSON data and managed through `StatusEffectQueue`; the runtime is owned by the turn-battle mod (`turn_battle_base`) and keyed per character via `StatusEffectService`, so the core character model stays free of battle state.

## JSON structure

```jsonc
{
  // Unique status effect identifier — used to look up and apply effects
  "Id": "stun",
  // Locale key for the effect's display name in tooltips and the status panel
  "Name": "status/stun/name",
  // Locale key explaining what the effect does
  "Description": "status/stun/desc",
  // Effect category: "Buff" (positive), "Debuff" (negative), or "Stun" (skip turn)
  "Type": "Stun",
  // Number of turns the effect lasts before expiring
  "Duration": 2,
  // Behaviour set ID — resolved via StatusEffectActionFactory into IStatusActions
  "Actions": "stun",
  // Icon filename loaded from the characters mod group
  "Icon": "stun"
}
```

## Field reference

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Id` | string | Unique effect identifier |
| `Name` | string | Locale key for display name (shown in tooltips and status panel) |
| `Description` | string | Locale key explaining what the effect does |
| `Type` | string | `"Buff"`, `"Debuff"`, or `"Stun"` |
| `Duration` | int | Number of turns the effect lasts before expiring |
| `Actions` | string | Behaviour set ID, resolved via `StatusEffectActionFactory` into an `IStatusActions` instance |
| `Icon` | string | Icon filename loaded from the `characters` mod group |

## Status effect types

| Type | Description |
|---|---|
| `Buff` | Positive effect that benefits the bearer (e.g. stat boost, regeneration). Rendered with a friendly tint in the UI |
| `Debuff` | Negative effect that harms the bearer (e.g. damage over time, stat reduction). Rendered with a hostile tint |
| `Stun` | Crowd-control — causes the bearer to skip their turn. Checked by the battle engine via `StatusEffectQueue.HasStun()` |

## Status effect file format

Status effect files are self-describing envelopes routed by `Kind`, with no
index file:

```jsonc
{
  "Kind": "status_effect",
  "Items": [
    {
      "Id": "effect/physics/stun",
      "Name": "status/",
      "Description": "",
      "Icon": "characters/effects/stun",
      "Type": "Stun",
      "Duration": 3,
      "Actions": "basic/stun"
    }
  ]
}
```

## Runtime behaviour

- Each battle combatant gets a `StatusEffectQueue` from `StatusEffectService.Of(character)` — an ordered list of active status effects
- `RemainingTurns` decrements in both turn phases: in `OnTurnStart` (only for timed effects with `Duration > 0`) and unconditionally in `OnTurnEnd`
- When `RemainingTurns` reaches 0, natural expiry fires `OnFinalAction`; manual removal via `Remove()` fires `OnRemove` instead
- The battle engine checks `HasStun()` to skip a stunned character's turn
- Effect behaviour callbacks are provided by `IStatusActions`, resolved from the `Actions` field via the factory

## StatusEffectQueue API reference

The queue lives in `mods/turn_battle_base/src/StatusEffect/StatusEffectQueue.cs` (namespace `Cthangover.Core.Cards.StatusEffect`). It is not a field of `Character` any more: `StatusEffectService.Of(character)` returns (and lazily creates) the queue from a `ConditionalWeakTable`, so queues die with their characters and the core model never references battle types. Battle code must go through the service instead of a `character.StatusEffectQueue` property.

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| `ActiveStatusEffects` | Defensive copy of the internal effect list (a new `List` per access) — safe to enumerate, external code cannot mutate the backing store |
| `Add(string statusEffectId, int duration = -1)` | Resolves the ID via `StatusEffectInfoFactory`, constructs a `StatusEffectItem`, fires `OnApply`, and appends it. Returns `false` when the factory lookup fails. A positive `duration` overrides both `Duration` and `RemainingTurns` from the definition |
| `Remove(string statusEffectId)` | Removes the first effect matching the ID, firing `OnRemove` first. Returns `false` if nothing matched |
| `HasStun()` | `true` if any active effect has type `Stun` — checked by the battle engine to skip turns |
| `OnTurnStart()` | Fires `OnTurnStart` on each effect, decrements `RemainingTurns` for timed effects (`Duration > 0`), and expires at zero via `OnFinalAction` |
| `OnTurnEnd()` | Fires `OnTurnEnd` on each effect, decrements `RemainingTurns` unconditionally, removes expired effects via `Remove` (which also fires `OnRemove`) |
| `OnDealDamage(Character target, ref int damage)` | Pipes outgoing damage through every effect's `OnDealDamage` hook, in insertion order |
| `OnTakeDamage(Character source, ref int damage)` | Pipes incoming damage through every effect's `OnTakeDamage` hook |
| `ClearAll()` | Fires `OnRemove` on each active effect, then clears the list |
| `Copy(Character newOwner)` | Builds a new queue bound to `newOwner`; each effect is cloned via `Copy()` and `OnApply` is re-fired in the new owner's context |

Timing semantics worth knowing:

- `IStatusEffect.Duration <= 0` means the effect never expires naturally — only `Remove()` or `ClearAll()` ends it
- `StatusEffectItem.RemainingTurns` is tracked independently of the definition's `Duration`, so the original value survives for display or re-apply logic
- `StatusEffectItem.Copy()` is a shallow clone: primitives are copied while the stateless `Actions` singleton is shared by reference

Built-in behaviour sets live under `mods/turn_battle_base/src/StatusEffect/Impls/` — e.g. `StunStatusEffect` (`ID = "basic/stun"`) implements every `IStatusActions` hook as a no-op, because stun is detected via `HasStun()` rather than through action callbacks.

## Implementing custom status effect behaviour

Create an `IStatusActions` implementation. Registration is fully automatic: the `StatusEffectActionFactory` constructor calls `Reflections.FindAndCreate<IStatusActions>()`, which scans every assembly loaded in the AppDomain (mod assemblies included) — no manual registration is needed:

```csharp
public class PoisonStatusActions : IStatusActions
{
    // Mandatory factory key matching the JSON "Actions" field (e.g. "basic/stun")
    public string ID => "basic/poison";

    public void OnApply(Character target) { /* called when effect is applied */ }
    public void OnTurnStart(Character target) { /* start-of-turn tick: DoT, regen */ }
    public void OnTurnEnd(Character target) { /* end-of-turn hook */ }
    public void OnDealDamage(Character source, Character target, ref int damage) { /* amplify/reduce outgoing damage */ }
    public void OnTakeDamage(Character target, Character source, ref int damage) { /* amplify/reduce incoming damage */ }
    public void OnRemove(Character target) { /* manual removal (cleanse) */ }
    public void OnFinalAction(Character target) { /* natural expiry */ }
    public void ModifyAttributes(CharacterAttributes attributes) { /* passive stat modifier */ }
}
```

The mandatory `string ID` property is the factory key matched against the effect's `Actions` field.

## Locale keys

```properties
status/stun/name = Stunned
status/stun/desc = Character skips their next turn
```

# Launching, testing and diagnostic tools

Use Godot 4.6 .NET and .NET 8. `dotnet build Cthangover.csproj` builds the kernel only: sources under `mods/` compile at runtime with Roslyn. A successful kernel build does not prove that mod compilation succeeds.

## Choosing a game or scene

Godot user arguments follow the separator `--`:

```text
godot --path . -- --game=novel_template --new
godot --path . -- --game=rpg_plus --load=slot_1
godot --path . -- --game=junior_reaper_paper_grief --new
godot --path . -- --game=rpg_plus --new --with-mods=rpg_object_editor --studio
```

| Argument | Effect |
|---|---|
| `--game=<collection_id>` | Load that game's mod set and enter it |
| `--new`, `--load=<slot>` | Start fresh (also the default) or load the game's save |
| `--with-mods=a,b` | Add the named mods and required dependencies for this run |
| `--all-mods` | Load all ordinary installed mods, overriding game/frontend selection; fixtures and inactive suites stay excluded |
| `--frontend` | Force the menu/mod-manager set when no explicit game or all-mods selection wins |
| `--scene=<logical_id>` | Navigate after boot to a registered logical scene; unknown IDs log an error and retain normal launcher behaviour |
| `--tile-renderer=topdown` / `isometric` | Override the collection's tile renderer |
| `--studio` | Open Scenario Studio when available |
| `--hot-reload`, `--no-hot-reload` | Override the editor/default file-watching policy |
| `--wait-for-debugger` | Show the attach-debugger dialog before boot |

With no game or development flag, only the frontend is loaded. Development flags (`--scene=`, `--itest=`, `--run-tests`, autoplay, atlases, debugger) imply all-mods when no game or frontend is selected. `--all-mods` takes precedence, then `--game=`, then `--frontend`, then the development fallback. An actual `.tscn` path is Godot's positional main-scene argument, not a logical `--scene=` value.

## Unified runner

```text
dotnet run --project tests/Cthangover.TestRunner -- --list
dotnet run --project tests/Cthangover.TestRunner -- --test unit
dotnet run --project tests/Cthangover.TestRunner -- --test mod_units
dotnet run --project tests/Cthangover.TestRunner -- --test resource_atlas
dotnet run --project tests/Cthangover.TestRunner -- --test locale_atlas
dotnet run --project tests/Cthangover.TestRunner -- --test coverage
dotnet run --project tests/Cthangover.TestRunner -- --json test-results.json
```

No selection runs the complete manifest: kernel build, xUnit and integration tests. `--no-build` skips the kernel build. Test IDs, scenes, arguments and window requirements live in `tests/tests.manifest.json`; logs go to `tests/artifacts/logs/<test>.log`. Exit 0 means the selected checks passed. Pure xUnit tests live under `tests/Cthangover.Tests`; mod units use each manifest's `test_sources`, compiled into a separate test assembly.

Direct mod testing uses `--run-tests [--mod=<id>]`. GUI suites declared in `test_suites` mount as `<host>__<suite>` only when an activation prefix matches, or with `--with-test-suites`; ordinary games and `--all-mods` do not activate them. A fixture needs explicit `--with-mods=`. Windowed tests need a real renderer/display, including pixel, Live2D and editor screenshot checks.

## Autoplay and captures

`--choices=0,1 --timeout=30` mounts `dialog_base__autoplay`, advances text and chooses indexed answers. `--dialogs=N` finishes after N completed dialogs for hub games that never become idle. The result marker is `[TEST_RESULT]`; inspect error logs and runtime mod compilation, not only process exit.

`dialog_base__doc_shots` runs capture steps with a selected game, `--itest=doc_shots --doc-steps=<file> --shots=<directory>`. It can navigate scenes, operate dialogs and panels, drive keys/mouse and save actual runtime frames. `cthangover_game__site_shots` and `site/make-shots.ps1` provide the site's game frames. Keep source captures and analysis outside mod repositories; bundled documentation assets are selected runtime captures.

## Validator and atlases

`validator` checks data/scenario references, schemas, conditions and unknown parameters independently of the authoring windows. `resource_atlas` maps providers and consumers, detects foreign resources without a transitive dependency, unrelated providers of one key, and dependency-less patches; missing providers are warnings. It also scans map-owned event scripts and teleport links. `locale_atlas` maps declarations and references in all installed languages: undeclared keys, invalid text/encoding and contradictory declarations are errors; missing translations are warnings and retain fallback behaviour.

Direct flags `--resource-atlas` / `--locale-atlas` generate reports and quit. `--with-test-suites` includes inert test resources for a full audit. The locale editor consumes the atlas scan and writes translations into the owning mod's locale files.

In the shared `/workspace` environment, heavy or longer-than-about-30-second runs must use the existing Windows watcher: publish an atomic, uniquely named job with a Russian purpose, track it to `.exit`, and inspect its result/state/log. See the workspace's `watch/README.md`; do not start another watcher or infer success from a pending job.

## Screenshot colour pipeline

Keep the normal renderer and `rendering/viewport/hdr_2d=true`. Capture through `Cthangover.Mods.Interface.View.ViewportCapture.SavePng(viewport, path)` or `Take(viewport)`, disposing the returned image. HDR 2D viewport pixels are linear; saving them directly to PNG makes screenshots dark. The shared helper converts RGB to sRGB before 8-bit quantization and does not transform alpha. `Convert(Rgba8)` alone is insufficient. Do not change HDR, exposure, display colour profiles or rendering backend to compensate. Compare a trial capture before a batch. This requirement is also recorded in workspace and project `AGENTS.md`.
mods/time/index:
# Time System

The in-game clock tracks time progression and drives day/night lighting cycles. Time affects quest progression, character stats, and scene appearance via the `light_use_time` feature.

## Time data structure

Time is tracked in `TimeData` as a single tick counter, from which all other values are derived:

| Property | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Tick` | `long` field | Raw clock tick (increments by 1 per in-game minute) |
| `Years` | `int` | Current year |
| `Months` | `int` | Current month (0–11) |
| `Days` | `int` | Current day (0–29) |
| `Hours` | `int` | Current hour (0–23) |
| `Minutes` | `int` | Current minute (0–59) |
| `Text` | `string` | Formatted display string (`"HH:MM"`) |

### Time-of-day properties

| Property | Description |
|---|---|
| `IsMorning` | True between 06:00 and 09:59 |
| `IsDay` | True between 10:00 and 17:59 |
| `IsEvening` | True between 18:00 and 21:59 |
| `IsNight` | True between 22:00 and 05:59 |
| `Phase` | `PhaseType` enum: `Morning`, `Day`, `Evening`, `Night` |
| `Normalized` | Float hour of day — `Hours + Minutes / 60f`, range 0.0–23.983 — used by lighting shaders |

## Time phases

| Phase | Hour Range | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Morning` | 06:00–09:59 | Dawn lighting |
| `Day` | 10:00–17:59 | Full daylight |
| `Evening` | 18:00–21:59 | Dusk lighting |
| `Night` | 22:00–05:59 | Dark, lamp-dependent |

## Time advancement

- `TimeTickController` advances time on a real-time timer when enabled
- Scenario actions can manually set or advance time
- `TimeData.AddTick()` increments by one minute, recalculating all derived properties
- `TimeData.AddTime(years, months, days, hours, minutes)` advances by a specific amount

## Lighting integration

The `light_use_time` DSL command and `light_use_time` metadata field control time-of-day-driven lighting:

```scenario
light_use_time true
```

When enabled, the lighting shader reads `TimeData.Normalized` to adjust scene colour temperature and lamp intensity based on the time of day. The player's lamp (`LampData`) provides a radius and influence value that the shader uses as a light source during night phases.

In scenario metadata:

```yaml
scene: home_kitchen
priority: 10
light_use_time: true
---
# scenario body
```

## Saving

Time is persisted in save files as a `long` tick value. On load, all derived properties (hours, phases, etc.) are recalculated.

# Shops and trading

`trading` adds the entity kind `shop` and the action `trade.open`. Currency is an ordinary inventory item; the default is `money/coin`, defined by this mod. A shop has unlimited stock and no persistent stock state. Sold items do not become its new offers.

Put a shop in `shops/` and depend on `trading` and the mods owning its goods:

```json
{
  "Kind": "shop",
  "Items": [{
    "Id": "my_game/merchant", "Name": "my_game/merchant/name",
    "Currency": "money/coin",
    "Sells": [{"Item": "rpg_plus/elixir", "Price": 10}],
    "Buys": [{"Item": "rpg_plus/branches", "Price": 1}]
  }]
}
```

`Name` is a locale key. `Sells` lists what the player buys; `Buys` lists what the merchant accepts. Prices are positive integers per unit; prices below 1 are ignored. The example goods are owned by `rpg_plus_game`.

```scenario
action trade.open shop=my_game/merchant
end
```

The trade window has the merchant's offers on the left and the player's bag on the right. Pick an item, set the quantity with the slider, −/+, or All, and press Buy or Sell. Buy quantities are limited by available currency; sell quantities by the bag. Other bag entries cannot be sold here. Walking is blocked while trading; Esc closes the window.

RPG Plus supplies the concrete shop `rpg_plus/village_merchant` in `mods/rpg_plus_game/shops/village_merchant.json`. To extend an existing shop, use `patches/shop/<your_mod>.json` and a dependency on its owner. Offers have no declared merge key. To update one offer, supply an explicit operation such as `"Sells$add": {"$key": "Item", "$items": [{"Item": "rpg_plus/elixir", "Price": 12}]}`. A plain `$add` appends instead; see [Array patches](../patches/arrays-and-identity.md).

Only inventory changes persist, in the `items_base` save slot. Data Editor and the command palette consume `mods/trading/schemas/trading.json`; implementation is in `mods/trading/src/`.

# Wrappers — UI Templates

A mod can attach its own UI (panels, overlays, widgets) to the game shell in two ways:

- **Manifest `ui[]` entries** — the supported, declarative way. A mod declares panels and overlays in `manifest.json`; the kernel instantiates the corresponding `.tscn` scenes, anchors them to named slots, and (for panels) wires a toolbar toggle button.
- **Wrapper template files (`.wrappertmpl`)** — plain-text UI tree templates collected from mods. The collection pipeline still exists, but **nothing instantiates these templates automatically**; see [Wrapper template files](#wrapper-template-files-wrappertmpl).

The old `manifest.json → subscriptions` array (template + code fragment + trigger) is **no longer part of the manifest schema** and has been removed from the engine.

## Attaching mod UI — the `ui` manifest entries

Each entry of the manifest's `ui` array declares one GUI element. Two kinds exist:

- `"kind": "panel"` — button-toggled panel. The UI registry owns a toolbar button for it (declared in `button`) and is the only one allowed to change its visibility. Panels always live for the whole session.
- `"kind": "overlay"` — no button; the element's own code decides when it is visible (optionally auto-shown with `show_on_start`).

Real example — `mods/cooking/manifest.json`:

```jsonc
{
  "ui": [
    {
      "id": "cooking_workbench",               // Unique within the mod; doubles as the toggle target
      "kind": "overlay",                       // No toolbar button
      "scene": "home_kitchen",                 // Only available in this logical scene
      "slot": "ModLastPanel",                  // Anchor slot node in the shell
      "scene_path": "scenes/cooking_panel.tscn", // Mod-relative .tscn, loaded at runtime
      "once": true,                            // Lives for the whole application
      "show_on_start": false,                  // Waits for a toggle or its own code
      "priority": 10                           // Layer/order inside the slot
    },
    {
      "id": "ration_stats",
      "kind": "overlay",
      "scene": "home_kitchen",
      "slot": "Lastground",
      "scene_path": "scenes/ration_statistics_panel.tscn",
      "once": false,                           // Created on scene enter, freed on scene exit
      "show_on_start": true,                   // Shown as soon as the scene is entered
      "priority": 20
    }
  ]
}
```

A `panel` entry additionally declares its toolbar button — from `mods/cthangover_game/manifest.json`:

```jsonc
{
  "id": "map",
  "kind": "panel",
  "slot": "ModBeforeUIPanel",
  "scene_path": "scenes/ui/map_widget.tscn",
  "button": {
    "icon": "map",              // Icon name resolved through the UI icon factory
    "locale": "ui/map/title",   // Tooltip/title key from locale files
    "index": 10                 // Button position on the toolbar
  },
  "priority": 10
}
```

### Entry fields

| Field | Applies to | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | both | Unique within the owning mod; doubles as the runtime cache key and the toggle target (e.g. for `ui.toggle_panel`) |
| `kind` | both | `"panel"` (button-toggled) or `"overlay"` (code-controlled visibility) |
| `scene` | both, optional | Logical scene this GUI belongs to; the GUI is hidden when leaving it. Absent = scene-independent, lives for the whole session |
| `slot` | both | Name of the anchor slot node in the shell (e.g. `ModBeforeUIPanel`, `ModLastPanel`, `Lastground`) |
| `scene_path` | both | Mod-relative path to a `.tscn` scene, resolved through the runtime TSCN loader — see [Runtime TSCN Scenes](../scenes/tscn-runtime/) |
| `once` | overlay | `true`: the instance lives for the whole application; `false` (default): created on scene entry, freed on scene exit. Panels are always treated as `true` |
| `show_on_start` | overlay | `true`: shown as soon as its scene is entered; `false` (default): waits for a registry toggle or the element's own code. Ignored for panels |
| `priority` | both | Layer/order inside the anchor slot. Defaults to `10`; ordering ties between mods are broken by mod load order |
| `button` | panel only | Toolbar button declaration: `icon`, `locale`, `index`. Forbidden for overlays |

Entries are validated at startup by `UiRegistry.Initialize`; invalid entries are logged and skipped. Panels get their toolbar buttons from the toolbox (`ToolBox.ApplyPanelButtons`) and are toggled with `UiRegistry` toggles — the same mechanism the DSL action `ui.toggle_panel` drives (see [Scenario Actions](../scenes/scenarios/actions/)). The in-game map is itself a `panel` UI entry — see [Map & Travel Zones](../map/).

## Scene lifecycle hooks

To run logic when a scene is entered or exited, use the event mechanisms instead of the removed `subscriptions` array:

- `.scenario` scene events — see [Scenes](../scenes/) and [Scenarios](../scenes/scenarios/);
- the `[SceneEvent]` attribute for declarative C# hooks — see [Scene Event Metadata](../metadata/).

Both are composed into one synchronous chain by `SceneManager.ComposeEvents` on scene enter; subscribers run in priority order (0/5/10/30). For the event bus used inside those hooks, see [Event Bus](../events/).

## Wrapper template files (`.wrappertmpl`)

The engine still collects wrapper template files from mods:

```filestree
wrappers/
├── default.wrappertmpl
└── custom_layout.wrappertmpl
```

- `WrapperTemplateResolver` scans every loaded mod recursively for `.wrappertmpl` files and caches the result.
- The static `WrapperTemplates.Collect()` facade returns them as `WrapperDefinition` records (`ModId`, `Name` = filename minus extension, `Content` = raw text).

**Currently nothing consumes them.** There is no automatic instantiation on scene enter, no `{{USER_CODE}}` substitution, and no manifest field that would bind a template to a scene — that pipeline was removed together with the manifest `subscriptions` array. A mod (or a future engine feature) can still call `WrapperTemplates.Collect()` and instantiate the raw template text itself; the content is kept as a raw string because it is parsed at instantiation time, not JSON.

## Building mod UI from code — ModWidget

When creating UI components from mod C# code, inherit from `ModWidget` (`mods/ui_base/src/Base/Lists/ModWidget.cs`). It provides an idempotent `Construct()`/`Destruct()` lifecycle for UI built from code inside mods: `EnsureConstructed()` calls the abstract `Construct()` exactly once, and the virtual `Destruct()` is called automatically on `_ExitTree`. Usage = override `Construct()` and build your children there:

```csharp
public class MyUIPanel : ModWidget
{
    protected override void Construct()
    {
        var label = new Label { Text = "Hello from mod!" };
        AddChild(label);
    }
}
```

Call `EnsureConstructed()` before adding the widget to the tree (as `CardBattleCore` does), so its children are constructed exactly once regardless of how many times construction is requested.

# Mod Packaging — .zip Distribution

Mods can be distributed as `.zip` archives instead of loose folders. The kernel loads them identically — zip is just a transport format.

## When to use .zip vs folder

| Format | Use case |
|---|---|
| **Folder** | Local development. Instant iteration — edit files, reload game |
| **.zip** | Distribution. Share with players, upload to mod platforms, versioned releases |

## Directory structure inside the zip

The zip must have the same structure as a loose mod folder:

```filestree
my_mod.zip/
├── manifest.json
├── src/
│   └── MyCode.cs
├── scenarios/
│   └── my_scene.scenario
├── items/
│   └── rations.json
├── backgrounds/
│   └── my_bg.png
├── locale/
│   └── en.properties
└── ...                     # any other assets
```

The root of the zip IS the mod root — no extra wrapper folder.

## How the kernel loads zipped mods

1. On startup, the registered mod scanners (`UserDataModScanner` and `GameDirModScanner`) enumerate filesystem entries in their respective `mods/` directories — both folders and `.zip` files are returned as `DiscoveredModEntry` items
2. The `ZipModLoader` claims any entry path ending with `.zip` and creates a `ZipModFileProvider` — the archive is opened directly with `ZipFile.OpenRead`, building an O(1) entry lookup dictionary in memory without extracting files to disk
3. The mod is loaded as if it were a folder — `manifest.json` is read from inside the zip, sources compiled, assets discovered
4. Zip mods have the same dependency resolution and lifecycle as folder mods; deduplication priority is controlled by the scanner's `ModSourceRoot.Priority`, not by format type

See [Resources — Loaders](../../resources/loaders/) for details on how `ZipModLoader` and custom loaders work.

## Creating a .zip for distribution

From the mod's parent directory:

```bash
# From mods/
zip -r my_mod_v0.1.0.zip my_mod/
```

Or using the Python build script (add this to your mod's tooling):

```python
import shutil
import json

def pack_mod(mod_path, output_path):
    with open(f"{mod_path}/manifest.json") as f:
        manifest = json.load(f)

    name = manifest.get("name", mod_path)
    version = manifest.get("version", "0.0.0")
    archive = f"{output_path}/{name}_v{version}"

    shutil.make_archive(archive, "zip", mod_path)
    print(f"Packed: {archive}.zip")
```

## Testing a zipped mod

1. Place the `.zip` in `mods/`
2. Remove the source folder (or keep both — if both a folder and a zip share the same mod ID, only one loads: a higher version always wins regardless of enumeration order; when versions are equal the first-encountered entry wins within the same root priority, and a lower-priority root always loses)
3. Launch the game — the mod loads from the zip
4. Check the game log for any errors

## Mod versioning

Include a `version` field in `manifest.json` for proper version tracking:

```jsonc
{
  "name": "MyMod",                                         // Human-readable mod name
  "version": "1.2.0",                                      // Semver version for tracking and compatibility
  "author": "you",                                         // Author credit
  "description": "..."                                     // Short description of the mod
}
```

The kernel **does** enforce version deduplication — `ModRegistry.RegisterCandidates()` keys candidates by mod `Id`, so only **one** version of a given mod ever loads:

- Within the same root priority: a candidate with a **higher version replaces** the already-registered one (logged as a warning); an equal or lower version is **skipped with a warning** — for equal versions, first-encountered wins.
- A candidate from a **lower-priority root never replaces** one from a higher-priority source, regardless of version.

Use version numbers for player information and mod platform compatibility checks.

## Zip mod limitations

- **No hot-reload**: Editing files inside a zip requires repacking. Use folders during development
- **No filesystem paths**: `GetFileSystemPath()` always returns `null` for zip mods — Godot's `ResourceLoader` cannot load scenes or shaders directly from within a zip. Assets that require filesystem access (shaders, scenes) are extracted to the mod cache on demand
- **File size**: No hard limit on zip size, but the entry lookup dictionary grows linearly with the number of files — very large archives (>10,000 entries) may increase the initial dictionary build time

## Existing test zips

The project includes test zip mods in `mods/` — these demonstrate the zip loading system:

```filestree
mods/
├── test_mod.zip
├── test_mod_a.zip
└── test_mod_b.zip
```

These are minimal mods used in automated tests to verify zip loading works correctly.

# Discovery Registry — `ModDiscoveryRegistry`

The registry discovers concrete `IModScanner` and `IModLoader` implementations by reflection. `Initialize()` scans the assemblies available at initialization and can be called more than once. The assembly lifecycle registers later contributions with `RegisterAssembly(assembly)` and removes them with `UnregisterAssembly(assembly)`.

| API | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `Scanners`, `Loaders` | Return thread-safe snapshots in registration order |
| `FindScanner(url)`, `FindLoader(url)` | Walk the corresponding snapshot in reverse registration order. Return the first strategy whose `IsCanProvide` accepts the URL, or `null` |
| `RegisterAssembly(assembly)` | Discover scanners and loaders in that assembly |
| `UnregisterAssembly(assembly)` | Remove the strategies owned by that assembly |

## Lookup during boot

`ModBootPipeline.PreparePaths` gets roots from each scanner and keeps a reference to the scanner that supplied each root. Boot runs that scanner for its own root and calls `FindLoader` for each entry. A strategy registered later becomes visible to subsequent lookups. The boot root list is captured during path preparation.

Loader order and source priority serve different purposes. Loader order selects a way to open one entry. Source priority and version decide which discovered candidate gets a shared ID. See [Resources](/docs/resources/) for the selection rules.
