# Resources — Pluggable Mod Infrastructure

The kernel separates discovery from file access. A scanner finds entries in a source, a loader opens an entry, and a provider exposes its files to the rest of the kernel.

```text
ModBootPipeline
  -> IModScanner: source roots and candidate entries
  -> IModLoader: open an entry
  -> IModFileProvider: read manifest.json and content
  -> ModRegistry: deduplicate IDs and select the active set
```

| Layer | Contract | Built into the kernel |
|---|---|---|
| [Scanners](scanners/) | `IModScanner` | Per-user directory and game directories |
| [Loaders](loaders/) | `IModLoader` | Directories, ZIP, and 7z |
| [Providers](providers/) | `IModFileProvider` | Directory and archive access, with a subdirectory view |
| [Discovery registry](discovery-registry/) | `ModDiscoveryRegistry` | Registration and strategy lookup |

## How precedence works

`ModDiscoveryRegistry.FindLoader` tries the last registered matching loader first. This controls how an entry is opened. If two entries have the same ID, discovery instead uses the source priority. The smaller number wins. At equal priority, the newer version wins. The first candidate stays when versions also match.

Discovery also checks each entry for a readable `manifest.json`. It can derive an ID from the entry name when a valid manifest omits `id`. Look in `MODS_REGISTRY` for invalid manifests and skipped or replaced candidates.

# Loaders — `IModLoader`

A loader opens a single entry discovered by a scanner. `IsCanProvide(url)` decides whether the strategy recognizes that entry. `CreateProvider` opens its storage and returns an [`IModFileProvider`](../providers/). The discovery pipeline owns that provider and disposes it if the candidate is skipped or replaced.

```csharp
public interface IModLoader : IModDiscoveryProvider
{
    IModFileProvider CreateProvider(string url, string modName);
    string GetFallbackModId(string url, string entryName);
}
```

| Built-in loader | Entry recognized | Fallback ID |
|---|---|---|
| `FolderModLoader` | Existing directory | Directory name |
| `ZipModLoader` | Case-insensitive `.zip` suffix outside existing directories | File name without extension |
| `SevenZipModLoader` | Case-insensitive `.7z` suffix outside existing directories | File name without extension |

The fallback ID applies only when a readable `manifest.json` omits its `id`. A directory named `example.zip` goes through the directory loader. ZIP and 7z loaders can obtain remembered credentials from the kernel's per-user archive password store (`user://archive_passwords.json`). Archive support is built into the runtime and requires no separate 7-Zip installation.

[Discovery registry](../discovery-registry/) describes how the kernel chooses a loader when several strategies match.

# Providers — `IModFileProvider`

The provider exposes a single storage root through mod-relative paths. The same interface serves manifest readers, the compiler, and resource loaders. The kernel accepts folder providers and archive providers for ZIP and 7z. `SubdirModFileProvider` restricts access to a subtree of an existing provider.

| Member | Contract |
|---|---|
| `Mod`, `RootPath` | Storage identifier and backing filesystem path, when one exists |
| `FileExists(path)` | Test for a file at a relative path |
| `ListFiles(directory)` | Enumerate immediate children. Directory names end in `/`, and hidden entries are omitted |
| `ReadFileText(path)`, `ReadFileBinary(path)` | Read the whole file as UTF-8 or bytes. Missing files return `null` |
| `OpenStream(path)` | Open a caller-owned stream. An archive stream may only support forward reads |
| `GetFileSystemPath(path)` | Return a physical path when one is available. Archive providers return `null` |
| `ResolveIncludePath(includePath, currentPath)` | Resolve an include relative to its source file |
| `Dispose()` | Release the provider and any open backing archive |

Close streams before the provider is released. For large files, use `OpenStream` when the consumer supports streaming. When processing a group of archived files, the kernel's archive providers also implement `IModFileSequence.VisitFiles` for sequential reads. A consumer that requires a physical filesystem path must account for archive entries.

# Scanners — `IModScanner`

Scanners identify source roots and enumerate possible mod entries. `IModScanner` extends `IModDiscoveryProvider`, which supplies a diagnostic `Name` and `IsCanProvide(url)` to test availability.

```csharp
public interface IModScanner : IModDiscoveryProvider
{
    IEnumerable<ModSourceRoot> GetRoots();
    IEnumerable<DiscoveredModEntry> Discover(string rootUrl);
}
```

`ModSourceRoot` contains `Url` and `Priority`. `DiscoveredModEntry` contains `Url`, passed to the loader, and `EntryName`, used for diagnostics and fallback ID selection.

## Built-in scanners

| Scanner | Runtime roots | Priority |
|---|---|---|
| `UserDataModScanner` | The absolute path for `user://mods/` | 0 |
| `GameDirModScanner` | `mods/` and, when present, `mods_private/` under the project or next to the exported game | 1 |

Outside Godot, the game-directory scanner emits relative locations with priority 0. The user scanner emits `user://mods/` literally in that context. Its availability check requires an actual directory.

## When scanners run

`ModBootPipeline.PreparePaths` collects the roots from every registered scanner on the Godot thread. `DiscoverAndCompile` then checks `IsCanProvide` and calls `Discover` on the scanner that supplied each available root. The directory scanners enumerate immediate children. Discovery skips hidden entries and hands the remaining URLs to the [loader registry](../discovery-registry/). For tools that need the currently accessible roots without running boot, use `ModRoots.ResolveModsRoots()`.
